The greatest risk is not wholesale replacement by AI, but the loss of routine operations work to network management automation and autonomous networks, combined with rapid shifts between technology generations. Planning and fault-isolation skills are becoming even scarcer.

No matter how intelligent the tools become, specialists still decide which links need more capacity, how to execute incident-free cutovers, and how to calculate capacity. Their judgment, signatures, and accountability remain indispensable in communications.

In one sentence: the future needs fewer people who can run inspections and more telecommunications engineering specialists who understand planning, execute stable cutovers, and calculate capacity accurately.
